content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces a data generation based method for few-shot object detection (FSOD) task. The key idea is using a VAE model to generate region proposal features whose norms are correlated with the overlap between the region proposals and the objects. And the VAE model is conditioned on the semantic embedding of each class, e.g. CLIP embeddings of class names. When finetuning on the novel set, the features from the ground truth are combined with the generated features under different IoU to mitigate the challenge of limited training data. Experiments show that the VAE generated features can improve the novel object detection accuracy at low-shot conditions (K < 10), especially on AP 50 ~ 75.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
# Strengths
+ This paper brings attention to increasing the variability related to the region proposal overlap with objects, which is an under-explored area for FSOD task. This makes the model robust to different region proposals of the same object.
+ The paper is well written.  Key ideas are easy to follow. 
# Weaknesses
- The method is claimed to be compatible with any two-stage object detection methods, but only the performance on DeFRCN is reported. Can the method also improve other FSOD detectors?
- In few-shot classification, previous works (e.g. Xu & Le, 2022) also used conditional VAE to generate representative samples, which undermines the novelty of this paper.
- The proposed method is mostly effective when K < 10. For K \ge 10, the improvement is marginal. It is better to provide some analysis for the reason, e.g. looking at the predicted detection boxes after NMS. Because NMS will remove the boxes highly overlapped with the final box, even if they have high confidence scores.
- In Table 3, it seems VAE with original data contributes most to the performance improvement. There lacks enough explanation for that.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: 8/10, writing is good.

Quality: 6/10.

Novelty: 5/10, connecting the feature norm with IoU score is somewhat novel.

Reproducibility: 6/10, may be reproducible by a researcher experienced with VAE and object detection.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall this paper is above borderline. See the Strengths and Weaknesses for details.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: To tackle few-shot object detection, this paper proposes norm-VAE  which is capable of generating data with increased crop-related variability. The generated features by the proposed norm-VAE is able to improve the performance of the classifier.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength

+ The proposed norm-VAE is simple and effective for feature generation.
+ The idea of using magnitude as IOU is interesting.

Weaknesses

- Lack of analysis:
1) Why using magnitude as the IOU is representative for features with different IOU. For example, the same low-IOU from the same input feature can represent different locations of the cropped input which may be more important for detection? The motivation for rescaling the norm is missing.
2) The further analysis of norm-VAE is missing. For example, why would the generated features improve the model? Could norm-VAE generate false positives or noisy features?
- Limited contribution and novelty:
1) norm-VAE is effective for feature augmentation and achieves best results built on top of DeFRCN. However, the contribution is limited to extend the model for feature augmentation.
2) The idea of rescale or cropping is very similar to random cropping augmentation. The main idea may not be new.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Paper is clear. Quality is on the borderline. Novelty seems weak. Reproducibility unknown.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper proposes a simple yet effective norm-VAE. The idea of represent IOU as magnitude is interesting. However, the contribution of this paper is limited. I would stand on the borderline for this paper temporarily.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

display_title: Official Review of Paper3378 by Reviewer dSii

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a method of data augmentation for few-shot object detection. The idea is to increase the variability of object crops by changing their ROI-pooled features based on the IoU with a ground-truth. The authors propose to match the norm of the ROI-pooled features to the IoU with the GT. They use a conditional VAE to generate the variations of the features. This allows them to generate additional features which can be used as augmentation during training object detectors.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The main strength of the paper is the idea of associating norm of features with IoU of the proposal with a ground-truth box. The authors propose to modify a detected ROI-pooled feature based on the IoU. This is an interesting idea and has not been explored before. 

However, the current version of the paper suffers from significant weaknesses and needs major revisions before it is ready for acceptance. Here are the most important weaknesses. 

1. Writing and notation. The paper writing needs to be improved to make it more readable and clear. In particular, I would like to point out that the authors might want to use a different notation for the number of object instances ($N$) to avoid confusion with the super-script used for novel classes ($C^N$).

2.  There are several decisions in the paper which need further explanation. For example, why is $g(.)$ chosen to be a linear transformation? Can we use a non-linear transformation and obtain improved results? Also, what is the significance of selecting $g(.)$ such that $g(1) = \sqrt{512}$ and $g(0.5) = 5*\sqrt{512}$? How are these selected?

3. In section 5.1, the authors mention that they used 60 categories disjoint from VOC as base classes and the remaining 20 as the novel classes. Are these 20 the same as PASCAL VOC classes? Or are there any other disjoint classes?

4. Lack of empirical evidence for more recent object detectors and object detection datasets. The authors should use more recent transformer-based object detectors (e.g. DETR) to demonstrate if the proposed approach can be extended to those. Further, the authors should show whether the proposed approach can work for large-scale datasets like LVIS - which are better suited for studying few-shot object detection.

5. It's not clear to me how are the semantic class features obtained used in the VAE. Is the VAE used during inference also? How? If yes, how are the class features $a$ obtained? Object detection is the task of localizing and recognizing objects. It's not clear if the authors are assuming knowledge of the class during inference. The authors should add a more detailed description of the inference process to the revision.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper can be improved significantly with clearer writing and explanations. The experimental quality can also be further improved by using more recent object detectors and better datasets. The idea of using a VAE to modify the norm of a feature is novel and can be a good contribution if the paper writing is improved and more empirical evidence added.
content.summary_of_the_review: I believe that even though the idea proposed in the paper is novel, the paper writing itself needs significant improvements. Therefore, I am recommending rejecting the paper at this venue to allow the authors to improve it and submit it again at another venue.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper targets few-shot object detection and proposes a generative-based approach based on the faster-rcnn framework. A very important motivation is that the model may fail to recognize the same object but with a different crop. A VAE-based generator is then proposed to generate features with the diverse region crops. The author uses the feature norm to indicate the region crop and the VAE is then trained to generate features under different norms. The reason for using norms as feature crop is motivated by the IoU between proposal and groundtruth bounding box. The experimental study provides promising performance.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1.	An effective generative approach for FSOD
2.	The motivation & observation is very important.
3.	Promising results and detailed ablation study.

Weakness:
1.	Though I may be wrong, I don’t think DefRCN uses FPN. As such, if the author uses DefRCN as baseline, the author should ensure the implementation details for fair comparison.
2.	I still cannot fully understand why the norms can be used to represent different features. If IoU is the only reason, one necessary comparison is to only generate features with low (or high) norm and then check the performance for better illustration.
3.	A few visualization between feature norm and IoU should be provided.
4.	Besides norm, is there any other property of features can be used? It is necessary and helpful for your approach design.
5.	What is the semantic embedding? I didn’t find the detailed explanation in the implementation details.
6.	Whether this approach can be generalized to TFA? After all, DefRCN has too much variants compared with TFA. As such, performance on TFA is necessary.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The motivation is important but part of the design in the approach is counter-intuitive. More analysis should be done for comprehensive & fair comparison.
content.summary_of_the_review: Please see the weakness & strength part.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
